turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes. Owen found out about this zero on his phone, in the middle of your class. Start with why nobody called me first.
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.
A machine's guess is not a finding. Even the company that sells that checker says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. What else do you have, Hale?
I don't need more proof than that.
Then you're telling me the zero stands on a percentage. Owen had no call, no chance to explain, and no note from you before it went into the gradebook. Who decided that was enough?
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
My child never lies. I'm writing down that you just compared him to a machine, and I'll want that in an email. Who decided, Hale, and on what basis?
Then I'm going upstairs to the principal before my 4:40 call. Put the zero on hold in writing before I leave, or the principal hears about it from me first.
